title: Medtrum CGM
body:
Dear Sir/Madam,

I have been using the Xdrip through Blucon/Ambrosia which has been great. I am of today picking up a new CGM through a Company called Medtrum UK

http://www.medtrum.com/S6.html

Can you confirm please if I can use this new device through Xdrip?

Many thanks for your help.

comments.body: It doesn't currently work with xDrip. To make it work we would basically need to have physical access to a device to reliably implement support for it. Is the unit you are receiving promotional? Do you think the manufacturer would be interested in xDrip being able to support it?

Hi I have bought 4 Sensors and a Transmitter for £225 the sensor lasts for 7 days and the transmitter is rechargeable bud, The reports and layout is very simuliar to Bluecon it provides a service but not as in depth as the xdrip provides, My contact there is a lady called Yadi and she is the Marketing and Sales Manager her email address is `email address removed`
It would be great if you could contact them as the product that you have is a great piece of kit, Please let me know how you get on and i will also try and contact her. I know that the Company are trying to get a CE mark for there next project which is a CGM that will last for 14 days. Hope this helps Bud. Paul
Hi have you spoken to the guy's from Medtrum?
Kimber can you post a review of your experience at FB group named Trials for diabetes please?
@kimbersdiabetic I sent them an email but haven't heard anything. Is it the S6 or A6 unit?

Hi Jamorham have you had any luck yet please with the guys at Medtrum.

On another topic what is the difference between Xdrip+ on my Android phone through Ambrosia and Xdrip+ Nightscout? Many thanks.

@kimbersdiabetic I haven't had any response to my April 30th email. Perhaps as a customer you could convince them to engage with me. I'm sure it is in their interest to do so but they might see things differently of course...
Leave it with me Bud, Whats the difference between Xdrip+ on my Android phone through Ambrosia and Xdrip+ Nightscout? Many thanks.

@kimbersdiabetic I don't really understand your last question. Ambrosia make the blucon device which can be used as a collector with Libre. xDrip+ is published by the Nightscout foundation but also "Nightscout" would often be used to refer to the Nightscout web service which xDrip+ can upload and download data from.
